overview:
Students interested in computer architecture, robotics, embedded systems, software-hardware interaction, computer hardware, and intelligent technologies frequently travel to Canada. In Canada, computer engineering integrates computer science and electrical engineering concepts to create, develop, test and enhance computer systems.

Depending on their prior credentials and professional aspirations, students can pursue undergraduate or graduate degrees. Engineering labs, research projects, design courses, and, at some schools, co-ops are among ways that Canadian universities provide learning opportunities.

Edu Hawk worldwide consultancy assists students in exploring international study options, comprehending university admission standards, and getting ready for the overseas education journey..

faq.question: After Class 12, are Indian students able to pursue computer engineering studies in Canada?
faq.answer: Indeed. After Class 12, Indian students who fulfill the academic requirements of the university which often include mathematics, physics, and occasionally chemistry can apply to undergraduate computer engineering programs.

faq.question: How long do computer engineering courses last in Canada?
faq.answer: The majority of undergraduate degrees in computer engineering take four years to complete. Depending on the university and whether the program is course-based or research-based, postgraduate master's programs typically last one to two years.

faq.question: What distinguishes Canadian computer science from computer engineering?
faq.answer: Indeed. Computer hardware, digital systems, embedded technologies, and the combination of hardware and software are the main topics of computer engineering. Although certain topics overlap, computer science places a greater emphasis on algorithms, software, computation, and programming.

faq.question: How much does it cost Indian students to study computer engineering in Canada?
faq.answer: Undergraduate tuition may cost between CAD 35,000 and CAD 75,000 or more per year, while postgraduate tuition may cost between CAD 20,000 and CAD 60,000 or more, according to a general planning estimate. Living expenses are extra, and each institution has different actual prices. Question 5. After earning my computer engineering degree, can I get employment in Canada? Depending on their program, school, academic background, and current IRCC standards, some graduates may be eligible for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP). A work permit, job, or permanent residence are not always assured by a Canadian degree.
